sections.content: You know *atentamente* and the formal register from B2 Unit 14 (no *tú*, set phrases) and the polite imperfect from B2 Unit 2 (*Quería pedirle un favor*). A letter to an office puts them together in a fixed order. It opens by saying who you are writing to and why: *Me dirijo a ustedes para solicitar…*. It states the request, often with the polite imperfect: *Quería solicitar información sobre el trámite*. It refers back to the matter with *al respecto*, thanks in advance with *de antemano*, and closes with *Atentamente,*. Each part is short, and the register never slips into *tú*.

sections.title: The parts of the letter
rows: Me dirijo a ustedes para solicitar una cita previa.
Quería solicitar información sobre el trámite.
Les ruego que me indiquen los pasos al respecto.
Les agradezco de antemano su atención.

items.spanish: Me dirijo a ustedes para solicitar una cita previa.
items.english: I am writing to you to request an appointment.

items.spanish: Quería solicitar información sobre la licencia.
items.english: I would like to request information about the licence.

items.spanish: Adjunto el justificante de la tasa.
items.english: I enclose the proof of payment of the fee.

items.spanish: Les agradezco de antemano su atención.
items.english: I thank you in advance for your attention.

sections.content: English letters can open with "Hi" and still be polite. Spanish ones to an office cannot: use *ustedes*, never *tú*, and a set opening. Keep the present for the act of writing (*Me dirijo*, not *Me dirigí*). The polite imperfect softens your own request only: *Quería solicitar…* is a polite present, not a story about the past.
